channel.title: GM Research
channel.description: Daily intelligence briefings on markets, law, AI, biohacking, trading and more.

item.title: Morning Edge: BTC holds $60.8K as Fed hike odds stay near 98% and record ETF outflows cap rallies
item.description: Yesterday’s call holds: BTC is flat near $60.8K, December Fed hike odds sit near 98%, and the Nvidia SEC probe keeps AI leadership under pressure.

item.title: Precedent: Switzerland Approves 57 Partner Jurisdictions for Crypto Tax Data Exchange From 2028
item.description: Switzerland's Federal Council approved 57 jurisdictions for CARF crypto tax data exchange from 2028, while ASIC's digital asset platform consultation closes today.

item.title: Cortex: Google routes AI agents through MCP and CLI, not raw REST APIs
item.description: Workspace MCP servers and CLI go GA with an addendum that makes them the required agent path. Plus Anthropic's Skills over MCP beta and Chinese open-weight releases.

item.title: Alpha: Passive vs Aggressive Flow: who is resting and who is crossing the spread
item.description: Limit orders rest and supply liquidity; market orders cross the spread and take it. Know who initiated before you trust any delta, sweep or absorption read.

item.title: Morning Edge: BTC bounces to $60.7K, but Fed hike bets and record ETF outflows keep rallies sellable
item.description: Wednesday's dip to $57.2K was bought, but December rate-hike odds near 98% and a record $4.94B ETF outflow month keep the bias bearish into the US holiday.

item.title: Precedent: Ukraine Passes Crypto Tax and Licensing Law as Senate Democrats Target SEC Rules
item.description: Ukraine's parliament passed a crypto bill with 271 votes, pending presidential signature; Senate Democrats demand the SEC rescind its crypto rules and exemption.

item.title: Cortex: Amazon's reported $7.5B Decart deal goes official; Anthropic ships Claude Ship
item.description: Amazon announces an agreement for Decart's core software and founders. Anthropic launches Claude Ship and Skills over MCP, and an unreleased Opus 5.6 surfaces in Claude Code.

item.title: Biohacker: Hypertrophy tracks weekly sets more than training frequency in 16 volume-matched trials
item.description: A preprint pooling 16 volume-matched trials finds frequency adds little to hypertrophy at equal weekly sets; also sleep and organ ageing, and keto vs Mediterranean for liver fat.

item.title: Alpha: Absorption: when aggressive orders hit a level and price refuses to move
item.description: Passive limit size soaks up market orders at a level. Delta shows the attack, and a reversal only counts once the aggressor runs dry. BTC's 20 Nov low is the live test case.

item.title: Rabbit Hole: Why Hot Water Can Freeze First, and Why Nobody Agrees Why
item.description: A 2,500-year-old observation, a schoolboy's ice cream, and a physics debate that still has no settled answer.

item.title: Morning Edge: BTC slips to $59.1K as Nvidia's rebound unwinds and Fed hike bets hold
item.description: Yesterday's thesis is playing out: BTC lagged the equity bounce and broke $60K, while semis gave back Monday's rally. December hike odds stay high.

item.title: Precedent: South Korea Unveils Digital Asset Act to Lift ICO Ban and Cap Exchange Stakes
item.description: The bill would end a nine-year ICO ban, cap exchange shareholders at 20%, and make crypto firms liable for customer losses from hacks.

item.title: Cortex: Amazon agrees to buy Decart's chip-optimization stack in a reported $7.5B deal
item.description: Amazon's reported $7.5B Decart deal targets Trainium efficiency against Nvidia. Also: Sierra's $30B raise, Poppy 1.0 for agent access, and an Asian AI-stock sell-off.

item.title: Praxis: Knowing more is not the bottleneck; reviewing what you did with it is
item.description: Clear on reflection, Mollick on AI's jagged capability and Housel on lopsided feedback all point to a deliberate weekly review loop.

item.title: Alpha: Bid/Ask Imbalance: the near book can lean bid while the tape keeps falling
item.description: Imbalance measures which side of the order book holds more resting size. It is a context reading on posted intent, not a forecast. Confirm it with executed flow.

item.title: Rabbit Hole: The Traffic Jam That Needs No Cause — and Travels Backwards
item.description: In 2008 a Nagoya team put 22 cars on a 230 m loop with no bottleneck and watched a jam form from ordinary human reaction delays.

item.title: Morning Edge: Nvidia rebound lifts stocks, but BTC slips to $60.4K as Dec Fed hike odds hold near 95%
item.description: Monday's Nvidia-led rally did not reach bitcoin, which slipped back to $60.4K. Yesterday's call that rallies are sellable holds for crypto; the S&P correction call has reversed.

item.title: Precedent: CFTC Lets Bitcoin, Ether and Stablecoins Count Toward Derivatives Operating Reserves
item.description: Staff advisory allows crypto, subject to haircuts, toward a year of operating costs; it is non-binding, and sources conflict on a separate event-contract rule.

item.title: Cortex: OpenAI and Cisco open-source Shirudo to shield unpatched Linux for AI agents
item.description: Shirudo lets agents draft temporary eBPF shields while patches roll out, but it is pre-release. Also: Claude Ship approval agents enter beta, and Z.ai ships GLM-5.4.

item.title: Biohacker: Yale 51-trial review: drugs and diet plus exercise beat supplements on biological age
item.description: A Nature Medicine analysis of 51 trials links metformin, semaglutide and combined diet and exercise to lower epigenetic age; over-the-counter supplements show little effect.

item.title: Alpha: Sweep Orders: one market order walks the book, and the gap it leaves is the signal
item.description: One marketable order walking several book levels in a burst. Urgency is the signal; the void it leaves and the next prints decide the read. BTC is testing this near $60k.

item.title: Rabbit Hole: The Moon Is Leaving Earth, and the Day Is Getting Longer
item.description: Mirrors left by Apollo astronauts show the Moon receding about 3.8 cm a year, with the energy taken straight from Earth’s spin.

item.title: Morning Edge: BTC rebounds to $61K, but Fed hike bets and S&P correction keep rallies sellable
item.description: A December Fed hike is priced near 92–97% and the S&P 500 is in correction. Bitcoin bounced to $61K from extreme fear, but ETF outflows keep the bear case intact.

item.title: Precedent: SEC Freezes $560M Backward Hat Crypto Ponzi Assets as Two Founders Are Arrested
item.description: The SEC and CFTC have filed parallel cases against Backward Hat Capital’s alleged $560M crypto Ponzi, with co-founders arrested and a receiver appointed.

item.title: Cortex: AI selloff: Nasdaq down 5.3% Friday as Anthropic gives back its IPO pop
item.description: Anthropic's ANT slid toward its $83 IPO price as the AI trade broke. OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol carry the model news, and Inkling 2 Mini leads open weights.

item.title: Praxis: The wealth and the future self you cannot see are the two things worth making visible
item.description: Housel's hidden wealth and Hershfield's future-self research converge: make the unseen concrete with a ledger, a progress log and a conversation with your older self.

item.title: Alpha: Spoofing & Iceberg Orders: the book you see is not the book that fills you
item.description: Spoofing shows size it never intends to fill; icebergs hide size behind small clips. Judge a level by what trades there, not by how big it looks.

item.title: Rabbit Hole: The Pistol Shrimp’s Snap Is a Bubble Dying, Not a Claw Closing
item.description: The sound comes after the claw has shut, when the cavity its water jet forged collapses, sending a shockwave and a brief flash of light.

item.title: Morning Edge: BTC clings to $60K as the S&P 500 correction and Nvidia’s SEC probe keep bear case alive
item.description: Friday’s US rout put the S&P 500 in correction and Nvidia down 14% on an SEC probe. BTC bounced to about $60K, but Fed hike bets remain the ceiling.

item.title: Precedent: Russia’s Crypto Trading Rules Take Effect Today as Licensed Operators Climb to 30
item.description: Bank of Russia ordinance permitting organized crypto trading starts 22 November, with 30 registered operators and a ₽300,000 annual retail cap.

item.title: Cortex: Claude-assisted Riemann hypothesis proof clears Lean checks as Mathlib backs it
item.description: A 17-million-line Lean proof of the Riemann hypothesis, built with Claude, passes independent checkers. Also: Kimi K3.1 Pro weights, Computer Use beta, Mistral's $110M round.

item.title: Biohacker: Plasma proteins track mortality in older adults; frequency matters less than volume
item.description: A 4,265-protein plasma screen linked to death risk in older adults, plus new evidence that weekly sets, not session count, drive hypertrophy. Evidence-graded.

item.title: Alpha: Footprint Charts: the bid and ask printed inside every candle
item.description: A footprint splits each bar into price levels and shows who hit the bid and who lifted the ask. Use it to confirm a level you already marked, not to call tops.

item.title: Morning Edge: BTC under $60K as Fed hike bets drag S&P 500 into correction
item.description: Yesterday’s BTC break is confirmed and extended: spot slid below $60K while the S&P 500 closed 3.7% lower in correction on AI and rate-hike fears.

item.title: Precedent: Judge Refuses to Block New York From Policing Kalshi, Leaving CFTC Preemption Unproven
item.description: A federal judge declined the CFTC's emergency bid to stop New York policing Kalshi's sports contracts, deepening the state-federal prediction-market split.

item.title: Cortex: DeepSeek raises about $15B in a second round as AI capital concentrates
item.description: DeepSeek's ~100B-yuan round dominated the day's AI funding. Also: Palo Alto's $4.5B Applied Compute deal, GPT-6.2 price cuts, and decentralized GPU forward markets.

item.title: Praxis: Your Leftover Hour Shows Your Real Ranking, and Time Is the Asset You Cannot Borrow
item.description: Seneca's letters converge: time is the only thing we truly hold, so whatever gets the leftover hour has already been ranked last.

item.title: Alpha: Liquidity Voids: when the book is empty, price skips levels and comes back
item.description: A liquidity void is a price zone with almost no resting size, so orders jump through it. Why BTC's slide below $60K ran through thin levels, and how to test a revisit.

item.title: Morning Edge: BTC breaks $63K as Fed hike bets firm and ETF outflows deepen
item.description: Yesterday's thesis is playing out: BTC is at $62,041 and Fear & Greed is at 10, while a December Fed hike is priced near-certain. Bearish lean into the 9 December FOMC.

item.title: Precedent: Utah Tells Court CFTC Cannot Upend Kalshi Loss as Prediction-Market Split Deepens
item.description: Utah's attorneys push back on the CFTC's bid to police sports event contracts as the Fourth Circuit split heads toward the Supreme Court.

item.title: Cortex: Anthropic closes its first Nasdaq session at $97.17, 17% above the $83 IPO price
item.description: ANT opened at $111.50, ranged $92.72–$115.10, and settled at $97.17. Also: Artificial Analysis now weights private tests at 60%, and Qwen3.8 still leads open-weight downloads.

item.title: Biohacker: A +120% training-volume jump did not beat +20% for muscle growth in trained lifters
item.description: Camargo et al. (J Appl Physiol, 2026): abrupt high-volume overload gave no extra hypertrophy, while protein-restriction and late-eating studies add longevity and metabolic angles.

item.title: Alpha: CVD: running tally of aggressive buying minus selling, and where it disagrees with price
item.description: Cumulative Volume Delta adds up market-order aggression bar by bar. Its real edge is divergence: when price makes a new extreme and the flow fails to confirm it.

item.title: Rabbit Hole: Old cathedral glass is not a slow liquid — the thick bottoms were made in the factory
item.description: The myth that medieval windows sag over centuries fails on viscosity. The real cause was crown-glass manufacturing and how glaziers set the panes.

item.title: Morning Edge: Nvidia beat fails to lift stocks as BTC slides below $64.5K and Fed hike bets firm
item.description: Yesterday's thesis reversed on price: Nvidia fell 2.9% after a record beat, BTC is near $63K, and December Fed hike odds sit near 88%.

item.title: Precedent: Fourth Circuit Rules States Can Target Kalshi’s Prediction-Market Event Contracts
item.description: The Fourth Circuit ruled on 17 November that states may target prediction-market event contracts, handing Kalshi its third federal appellate loss.

item.title: Cortex: Anthropic's ANT listing day arrives as Marvell agrees to a $115B Lumentum deal
item.description: Anthropic's Nasdaq debut today, the week's biggest deal (Marvell and Lumentum), decentralized AI token moves tied to IPO attention, and MCP becoming shared agent infrastructure.

item.title: Praxis: You cannot forecast the risk that hurts you, so design for the surprise instead
item.description: Housel's risk essays and Mollick's jagged-AI framing converge: when failure cannot be forecast, build margin and test by hand.

item.title: Alpha: Passive vs Aggressive Flow: which side of the book is absorbing the tape
item.description: Every trade pairs one aggressor with one resting order. Learn to read which side is winning at a level, using BTC's 18 Nov 2026 liquidation hours as the live example.

item.title: Rabbit Hole: Why about 30% of real numbers start with 1 — and how worn pages found the pattern
item.description: In 1881 an astronomer noticed his logarithm tables were worn at the front. The pattern became Benford's law, and today it flags fabricated data.
